title: Remediation — Fixing, Verifying and Prioritising

levels.beginner: Remediation is the work after a finding: understand the root cause, fix it at the right layer, prove the fix works, and make sure the same bug cannot come back quietly.
levels.intermediate: Prioritise by real risk, not only by score: exploitability (is it reachable? is there a public exploit? is it in CISA KEV?), exposure (internet-facing? sensitive data?), and blast radius. A medium bug on an internet-facing login page can matter more than a critical bug in an unused internal tool.
levels.advanced: Fix at the root-cause layer when you can (a shared validation library beats ten one-off patches), add a regression test that fails if the bug returns, and track the fix to closure with a due date — KEV entries even carry a due date for exactly this reason.

key_points: Prioritise by exploitability + exposure + data at risk, not score alone.
Fix the root cause at the shared layer where possible.
Add a regression test that fails if the bug returns.
Verify the fix in staging with the same test that found the bug.
Track remediation to closure with an owner and a due date.

defensive_examples.title: A remediation checklist for one finding
defensive_examples.code:
1. Reproduce the finding in a lab (never on production data)
2. Identify the root cause and the layer to fix
3. Fix + add a regression test
4. Re-run the original test — it must now fail to exploit
5. Review, deploy, and record closure with date + owner
defensive_examples.explanation: Step 4 is the one teams skip: without re-running the original test, you have a change, not a verified fix.

knowledge_check.question: A critical-severity bug sits in an unused internal tool, and a medium bug sits on the public login page. Which do you fix first?
options: Usually the medium bug on the public login page — it is reachable and exploitable
Always the critical one, scores decide everything
Neither — wait for the next release
The one with the shorter CVE ID
knowledge_check.explanation: Severity scores do not include your exposure. Reachability, exploitability and data at risk decide real priority.

knowledge_check.question: Why add a regression test as part of a fix?
options: So the bug is caught automatically if it ever comes back
Because tests are required for the CVE to close
knowledge_check.explanation: Without a regression test, a later refactor can silently reintroduce the same weakness and nobody notices until the next incident.
